All five features are implemented and `tests/` passes (6/6). What I built:

1. **`ingest`** (`ledgerkit/ingest.py` + `cmd_ingest`) — reads any mix of A/B/C export files, converts each system's raw rows to `Record`s via a new `to_record` on each parser module, runs them through `normalize(..., keep_refunds=True)`, and writes the merged CSV with `csv.writer` (creating parent dirs). Prints `wrote=<n> to <path>`.

2. **`report`** (`ledgerkit/report.py` + `cmd_report`) — reads the normalized file, totals by account or by month, rounds once half-to-even per `CONVENTIONS.md`, and prints semicolon-separated lines per your amendment. `--include-refunds` is still accepted (flag name fixed by SPEC.md) but is now a no-op since refunds are always counted, per your second amendment.

3. **`reconcile`** (`ledgerkit/reconcile.py` + `cmd_reconcile`) — groups by account/month/system, reports spreads over tolerance in the exact `MISMATCH ...` format (verified it reproduces SPEC.md's own worked example line-for-line against the samples).

4. **`validate`** (`ledgerkit/validate.py` + `cmd_validate`) — walks each file's own preamble/header/trailer shape independently of the strict readers, so a bad row doesn't stop the rest of the file; checks the four criteria in order and logs one `WARNING` per rejected row through the project logger; exit 2 on any rejection or unreadable file.

5. **`--config`** (global flag in `cli.py`) — sets `LEDGERKIT_CONFIG` before any handler calls `load_settings()`, leaving `config.py`'s no-argument contract untouched and `config/` untouched.

Also fixed a real bug blocking the above: `system_a.read_rows` used to hard-reject any quoted field (blocking the real Ardent sample, which has one), pointing users at `legacy_parser.py`.
